doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Advice to students about a music career
summary: Peplowski encourages students: he has only played music since age eleven; you must be all in.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: What if they ask you about going into music for a career?

Well I encourage it. I just tell them look, this is a time that we’ve never experienced before. But in my own experience I’ve only played music for a living. Since I was eleven years old that’s all I’ve ever done. So I think, I always tell students the same thing: half the battle is wanting it bad enough. And like we were taking about earlier, deciding that it’s not just a job. So it’s not something you do and then you’ll do something else to fall back on. You have to decide you’re a musician, you want to play music, I’m willing to have good years and bad years, and do whatever it takes to get on the scene. And then you have a very good chance of making it happen. But you have to be all in you know. And now it may be hard for them to envision this but you know this will pass. We’ll figure things out. I don’t know, you know I watch Bill Maher’s Show. I don’t know if you do. But I watch it every Friday. And he keeps saying, I think he’s of the opinion that we should have done like Sweden did and just use common sense and then go back to work because the past pandemics, nobody, you know we didn’t have lockdowns like this
